cohort: The study included 343 nulliparous Sudanese women who underwent primary cesarean section at Bashir Hospital (Riyadh district, Khartoum).
finding: Emergency cesarean section was associated with poorer neonatal outcomes, including significantly lower Apgar scores, higher frequency of low birth weight, increased NICU admissions, and neonatal mortality.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean section was associated with poorer neonatal outcomes, including significantly lower Apgar scores, higher frequency of low birth weight, increased NICU admissions, and neonatal mortality, compared to elective cesarean section.
gest_age: <37 weeks (identified as a predictor of low Apgar scores, with most deliveries at term)
